sections.content:
OK, now I see a new state for the bottom block:
- id=13: purple, 70 pixels - this is the main purple part
- id=14: white, 10 pixels - this is a small white triangle in the top-right corner
So when the room is rotated LEFT and I SPACE with purple, the bottom block becomes:
- Purple (70 pixels) with a small white triangle (10 pixels) in the top-right
This is different from all previous states. Let me track the pattern:
- When room is center, SPACE(purple) on State A → State B (purple 65 + white 35)
- When room is rotated LEFT, SPACE(purple) on State A → New state (purple 70 + white 10)
The white region is shrinking! From 15 pixels (State A) to 10 pixels. Maybe if I keep applying SPACE with purple in different orientations, the white region will shrink to 0, giving a fully purple bottom block?
Let me try SPACE with purple again, but this time with the room rotated RIGHT.

<function=python>
<parameter=code>
# Current: room rotated LEFT, purple; bottom: purple (70) + white triangle (10) top-right
# Let me try rotating RIGHT (two rotations from LEFT to get to RIGHT) and SPACE with purple

action(['RIGHT', 'RIGHT'])  # LEFT -> center -> RIGHT
after = current_frame.segmentation
print("After 2x RIGHT (room now rotated RIGHT):")
for n in after['nodes']:
    if n['id'] in [11, 12]:
        print(f"  id={n['id']}, color={n['color']}, pixels={n['pixels']}, boundary={n['boundary']}")

action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 4, 'col': 43}, 'SPACE'])
after = current_frame.segmentation
print("\nAfter SPACE (purple, room rotated right):")
for n in after['nodes']:
    if n['id'] in [12, 13, 14]:
        print(f"  id={n['id']}, color={n['color']}, pixels={n['pixels']}, boundary={n['boundary']}")
print(f"Level completed: {last_action_result.get('level_completed', False)}")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
